summary: 1936 plan for an 80-foot steel fire tower on U.S. 1 north of Aiken; the eastern lookouts record lists it as removed, with no date or site description found.

facts.status_note: Listed as removed on the eastern U.S. lookouts site; no removal date found.

events.note: State forestry commission bought a six-acre site on U.S. 1 north of Aiken for a planned 80-foot steel tower; the article describes it as still to be built.

evidence.supports: Agency is the South Carolina Forestry Commission
State commission bought a six-acre tract on U.S. Highway 1, 3 miles north of Aiken
evidence.quote: The State Forestry commission last week purchased a six-acre tract of land, located on United State Highway No. 1, 3 miles north of Aiken,

evidence.supports: Tower was to be the fifth steel tower in Aiken County, for the program to protect county forests
evidence.quote: for the purpose of erecting thereon the fifth steel tower to be built in Aiken county in the program to protect county forests against fires.

evidence.supports: Site is the highest point in Aiken County; tower to be erected, 80 feet in height
evidence.quote: The site occupies the highest point in Aiken County, and the tower to be erected will be 80 feet in height.

evidence.supports: Tower house and outbuildings for the towerman to be built on the same tract
evidence.quote: On the same tract will be built a tower house and the necessary outbuildings for the towerman.

evidence.supports: With the new tower the county will be well protected, alongside similar towers now at Wagener, Graniteville, Oskwood and Silverton
evidence.quote: similar towers now located at Wagener, Graniteville, Oskwood and Silverton.

evidence.supports: Towerman to be named once the tower is erected; district of Ranger U.G. Ouattlebaum, Monetta section
evidence.quote: The new tower is in the district of Ranger U.G. Ouattlebaum, of the Monetta section and a towerman will be named to have charge of the same as soon as the tower is erected.

evidence.supports: Eastern lookouts record marks the tower as removed
The Forestry Commission closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993
evidence.quote: The Forestry Commission closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993.

notes_for_editor: The only tower-specific source is a March 1936 newspaper report, quoted on the eastern lookouts page, that describes the tower as planned. Nothing read confirms it was built, how tall it stood, who staffed it, or when it came down; the removal label has no date. The height of 24.4 m is the planned 80 feet, not a measured height. The article says the site was three miles north of Aiken on U.S. 1, but the record coordinates (33.7509, -81.6431) do not obviously match that; not reconciled. A State Historic Property Record for a Monetta Lookout Tower on US 1 in Aiken County exists (schpr.sc.gov/index.php/Detail/properties/73577), but the fetch returned a verification page, which I did not pass; nothing from it is used. A human reader with access may find a current description there.
